'''Stéphane Mangin''' is a [[physicist]] and professor at the [[University of Lorraine]] in [[Nancy, France]]. He is head of the Nanomagnetism and [[Spintronic]]s group<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=SPINTEAM website|url=https://spin.ijl.cnrs.fr/|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=}}</ref> at the Institut Jean Lamour,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ijl.univ-lorraine.fr/en/a-la-une/|title=Institut Jean Lamour|last=|first=|date=|website=ijl.univ-lorraine.fr|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2019-04-27}}</ref> a laboratory jointly run by the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|CNRS]] and the University of Lorraine.

His research concerns the study of [[nanomagnet]]s and their [[magnetization dynamics]] under the influence of different stimuli such as a [[magnetic field]], a current pulse which can generate a [[spin-transfer torque]], a spin-orbit torque (see [[Spin–orbit interaction|spin-orbit interaction]]), or an [[ultrashort pulse laser]].

His work has had technological applications to [[magnetoresistive random-access memory]] (MRAM) and magnetic data storage on [[hard disk drive]]s, for example [[heat-assisted magnetic recording]] (HAMR) using a [[laser beam]].

== Biography ==
Stéphane Mangin obtained his [[PhD]] thesis in 1997 at the [[Joseph Fourier University|Université Joseph Fourier]] in [[Grenoble]], France, later becoming a post-doctoral researcher at the [[Université catholique de Louvain]] in Belgium. He was an assistant professor at the [[Henri Poincaré University]] in Nancy, before promotion to a full professorship in 2008.

He has worked in collaboration with many laboratories all over the world. In 2004–2005, he was an invited researcher at [[IBM Research – Almaden|Hitachi GST San Jose Research center California]] and in 2012–2013, an invited professor at the Center for Magnetic Recording Research<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cmrr.ucsd.edu/|title=CMRR|website=cmrr.ucsd.edu|access-date=2019-04-27}}</ref> in the [[University of California, San Diego]] (UCSD). In 2015, he co-founded an International Laboratory on NanoElectronics with [[Eric Edward Fullerton|Eric Fullerton]] at UCSD, Dafiné Ravélosona at [[Paris-Sud University]] and Andrew Kent at [[New York University]]. In 2021-2022, he had been a visiting fellow and professor at [[Churchill College, Cambridge|Churchill College]], [[University of Cambridge]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=People – Churchill College|url=https://www.chu.cam.ac.uk/people/view/stephane-mangin/|access-date=2021-09-19|website=www.chu.cam.ac.uk}}</ref>

Since 2009, he has been the scientific director of project Tube Daνm (Deposit and Analysis of [[Nanomaterials]] under [[Ultra-high vacuum|Ultra-High Vacuum]]), a 70-meter-long technological platform, the only such device in the world. This tube allows researchers and companies to work under ultra-high vacuum conditions in order to grow thin film material with new properties,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ijl.univ-lorraine.fr/en/research/competence-centers/deposit-and-analysis-of-nanomaterials-under-ultra-high-vacuum-daum/|title=Daµm Competence Center (Deposit and Analysis of Nanomaterials under Ultra-High Vacuum)|last=|first=|date=|website=|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref> allowing for example future data storage possibilities.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.cnrs.fr/videos/faster-and-greener-data-storage|title=Faster and Greener Data Storage|last=|first=|date=|website=CNRS News|language=en|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2019-06-18}}</ref>

He has organized or co-organized several international conferences and workshops, including the Magnetic Single Nano-Object Workshop and School<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://msnows2018.event.univ-lorraine.fr/|title=UniGR M-SNOWS 2018 Magnetic Single Nano-Object Workshop & School - Sciencesconf.org|website=msnows2018.event.univ-lorraine.fr|access-date=2019-04-27}}</ref> and the World Materials Forum.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=World Materials Forum|url=https://worldmaterialsforum.com|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=worldmaterialsforum.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zzDDTXB9oPw|title=World Materials Forum - Video|last=|first=|date=2019|website=[[YouTube]]|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref>

Mangin had actively engaged in interactions between science and the general public, including popularization and mainstream conferences.<ref>{{Citation|title=Stocker plus, plus vite et plus sobre|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fgboyssYsPQ|language=en|access-date=2021-09-19}}</ref> Between 2013 and 2019, he served on the committee of the "[[Parliamentary Office for the Evaluation of Scientific and Technological Choices]]", a French governmental advisory group.

== Honors and awards ==

* 2007: Junior member of the [[Institut Universitaire de France]]
* 2008: First research prize from the [[Lorraine]] region
* 2010: President of the local section of [[Société Française de Physique|Société française de Physique]]
* 2015: Member of the local section of the [[French Academy of Sciences]]
* 2017: Senior member of the [[Institut Universitaire de France]]
* 2018: Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]]
* 2019: President of [[IEEE Magnetics Society]] France Chapter
* 2021: IEEE Fellow of the [[IEEE Magnetics Society|Magnetic Society]]
* 2022: Visiting Fellow of [[Churchill College, Cambridge]]
* 2025: Member of [https://www.eurasc.eu/ European Academy of Sciences]<ref>{{Cite web |last=European Academy of Sciences |title=Members: Stéphane Mangin |url=https://www.eurasc.eu/members/stephane-mangin/member/}}</ref>
* 2025: [[Ordre national du Mérite|Chevalier de l'Ordre national du Mérite]] (nominated the 15 may 2025)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Décret du 15 mai 2025 portant promotion et nomination dans l'ordre national du Mérite |url=https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/jorf/id/JORFTEXT000051597789 |website=www.legifrance.gouv.fr}}</ref>
